guidance.summary: Palantir guided Q3 2026 revenue of $2.160–$2.164 billion and raised its full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($8.150–$8.158 billion), U.S. commercial revenue (over $3.424 billion), adjusted operating income and adjusted free cash flow, while continuing to expect GAAP profitability each quarter.

guidance.sentence: • Adjusted income from operations of between $1.292 – $1.296 billion.
• We are raising our revenue guidance to between $8.150 – $8.158 billion.
• We are raising our U.S. commercial revenue guidance to in excess of $3.424 billion, representing a growth rate of at least 134%.
• We are raising our adjusted income from operations guidance to between $4.889 – $4.897 billion.
• We are raising our adjusted free cash flow guidance to between $4.5 – $4.7 billion.
• And we continue to expect GAAP operating income and net income in each quarter of this year.

sentences: A reconciliation of non-GAAP guidance measures to corresponding GAAP measures is not available on a forward-looking basis without unreasonable effort due to the uncertainty regarding, and the potential variability of, reconciling items that may be incurred in the future, such as stock-based compensation and related employer payroll taxes, the effect of which may be significant.

writeup.headline: Palantir rates Buy: exceptional growth, margins and net cash offset a very high absolute valuation.
writeup.thesis: Palantir scores 70, a Buy, driven by near-perfect growth (98), with latest-quarter revenue growth of 92.8% year on year, TTM revenue growth of 78.9%, and growth sped up by 8.1 pp from the previous quarter. Quality is strong at 86, with an 84.8% gross margin, 42.8% operating margin, 54.5% FCF margin and diluted share count up 0.2% year on year, though stock-based pay is 13.6% of revenue. The balance sheet scores 100 on net cash, and the trend score of 79 reflects the price 28.3% above its 200-day average and shares 33.6 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Valuation is the drag at 8: in absolute terms the multiples are very high (P/S of 82.1x, P/FCF of 150.5x, EV/EBIT of 188.3x, FCF yield 4.3 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield), and it is expensive against its own history (EV/EBIT not comparable). News is mildly positive at 62, helped by upgrades and target raises.
key_risks: Very high absolute valuation leaves little room for any slowdown in growth
Q3 results due November 2 could disappoint against raised full-year guidance
European pushback on defence adoption and procurement scrutiny
Bearish analyst views persist, such as RBC's Sell rating
what_would_change: A drop of 6 points in the score, for example from weaker growth or a fading trend, would move it to Hold
A gain of 10 points would reach Strong Buy, most plausibly via a better valuation score if multiples compress while growth holds
A weak Q3 report or guidance cut would hurt growth, news and trend scores together
Negative news on European customers or regulation would pull the news risk score down
